request: Please find me data regarding first-of-class ship cost overruns

reply.reply:
**Useful first-of-class benchmarks include the Ford carrier’s final $13,316.5 million procurement cost and a frigate lead ship’s $1,499.3 million estimated cost; the excerpts do not quantify actual overruns against original baselines.**

- The lead ship had an estimated procurement cost of $1,499.3 million, higher than follow-on ships due to its learning-curve position and inclusion of much of the class's DD/NRE costs. (R44972, PDF p. 10)
- CVN-78 was procured in FY2008 and its final procurement cost was $13,316.5 million in then-year dollars. (RS20643, PDF p. 7)
- Reported weight growth suggests potential cost growth beyond the figures in the 2020 and 2023 CRS and CBO analyses. (R44972, PDF p. 39)

Not yet covered: The excerpts do not provide an original-versus-final baseline comparison for the carrier, so its overrun amount or percentage cannot be calculated here.; The frigate figure is an estimate, and the cited passage describes potential cost growth rather than a realized overrun.
reply.reasoning: Recent CRS reports provide lead-ship cost figures and explain why first ships may cost more, but the evidence captured does not establish realized overruns against original estimates.
